headline: Transfer, kernel and penalized methods raise power in genetic association studies
label: Genetic Association Power Methods
summary: Recent methods address power gaps in trans-ethnic, survival, longitudinal and epigenomic association studies.
synthesis: The common thread is using auxiliary information or flexible penalized and kernel models to raise power in genetic and epigenomic association and prediction. tranScore transfers EUR-EAS summary statistics via genetic similarity to strengthen East Asian GWAS. GWKBR adds GWAS-informed priors to a Bayesian kernel model for genomic prediction, and GEiPRS models genotype-environment interactions in penalized polygenic risk scores. Spectral components from identity-by-descent graphs adjust for fine-scale structure, outperforming PCs in UK Biobank. Kernel multi-marker accelerated failure time tests handle left truncation and competing risks, while waveome applies Gaussian-process variable selection to longitudinal omics counts. The new element is adaptation to ancestry, survival, and temporal structure rather than standard single-marker designs.
